# Introduction

This report imports a public Incucyte time-course screen into gDR. The data come from the
**HMS LINCS MCF10A common project** (Harvard Medical School LINCS Center): non-tumorigenic
mammary epithelial MCF10A cells expressing H2B-mCherry, imaged live in an Incucyte for five
days under eight drugs.

The experiment is `MN20160421` — six 384-well plates sharing one randomized layout, read every
four hours. Unlike the other examples in this repository, the readout is a **cell count per
well over time** rather than a single endpoint, so the pipeline runs in time-course mode.

```{r libraries}
library(qs2)
library(data.table)
library(summarytools)
library(gDRutils)
library(gDRimport)
library(gDRcore)
library(gDR)
library(gDRplots)


```

```{r get_wd}
wd <- getwd()
for (d in c("plots", "gDR_data", "tables", "data_annotation")) {
  dir.create(file.path(wd, d), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
}
prepared <- file.path(tempdir(), "prepared_input")
dir.create(prepared, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)


```

# What ships with this example

`raw_data/` holds the files exactly as published, unedited:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `MN20160421_X0{1..6} total.txt` | Incucyte exports, one per plate: a metadata preamble followed by one column per well |
| `Layout_20160421_308.tsv` | the plate map — drug, HMS LINCS id and concentration for each of 308 wells |
| `20160421_MCF10A LINCS_drug response live_plateID.tsv` | plate table — cell line, plating date, treatment start (`T0date`) and plating delay per barcode |
| `GRmetrics_1.tsv` | GR metrics published with the project, used for a qualitative cross-check in report 3 |

Everything gDR needs is derived from those four in this report — nothing was edited by hand.

# Preparing the instrument files

Two edits are needed before `gDRimport` can read the Incucyte exports. Both concern the
metadata preamble; the plate block itself is fine.

**A barcode row.** `load_results_Incucyte()` looks for a row whose first cell is `Barcode` and
takes the plate identifier from the cell next to it. These exports label the plate with
`Label: MN20160421_X01` instead, so the row has to be added. It cannot be the first line,
because `data.table::fread(header = TRUE)` reads line 1 as column names.

**Padding.** Each preamble line holds a single field while the data block holds 310. `fread`
treats the mismatch as a leading comment block and skips it, after which the loader no longer
finds its `Date Time` marker. Padding the preamble to the same field count keeps it visible.

```{r patch_headers}
patch_incucyte_header <- function(path, outdir) {
  txt <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  hdr <- grep("^Date Time", txt)[1]
  # count separators rather than strsplit() pieces: strsplit() drops a trailing
  # empty field, which would leave every padded line one short
  n_fields <- function(l) nchar(l) - nchar(gsub("\t", "", l, fixed = TRUE)) + 1L
  ncol <- n_fields(txt[hdr])
  label <- trimws(sub("^[^:]*:", "", txt[1]))

  pre <- append(txt[seq_len(hdr - 1L)], paste0("Barcode\t", label), after = 1L)
  pad <- vapply(pre, function(l) paste0(l, strrep("\t", max(0L, ncol - n_fields(l)))),
                character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)

  out <- file.path(outdir, basename(path))
  writeLines(c(pad, txt[hdr:length(txt)]), out)
  out
}

raw_files <- sort(list.files("raw_data", pattern = "total\\.txt$", full.names = TRUE))
results_files <- vapply(raw_files, patch_incucyte_header, character(1),
                        outdir = prepared, USE.NAMES = FALSE)
basename(results_files)


```

# Building the manifest and the template

The published layout is a long table — one row per well. gDR reads plate maps as positional
grids, so it is reshaped: the cell in sheet row *r* and column *c* describes the well in plate
row *r* and column *c*, with no row or column labels.

Two column names are reserved for pipeline output and cannot be used as inputs: `DrugName` as
a template sheet and `CellLineName` as a manifest column. The readable drug name therefore goes
into the drug identifier sheet (`Gnumber`), and the HMS LINCS id travels alongside as extra
well metadata.

```{r build_template}
layout <- fread("raw_data/Layout_20160421_308.tsv")
plate_tab <- fread("raw_data/20160421_MCF10A LINCS_drug response live_plateID.tsv")

n_row <- 16L
n_col <- 24L
grid_of <- function(values) {
  m <- matrix(NA_character_, n_row, n_col)
  m[cbind(match(substr(layout$Well, 1, 1), LETTERS),
          as.integer(substring(layout$Well, 2)))] <- as.character(values)
  as.data.frame(m)
}

is_vehicle <- layout$pert_type == "ctl_vehicle"
sheets <- list(
  Gnumber       = grid_of(fifelse(is_vehicle, "vehicle", layout$DrugName)),
  Concentration = grid_of(fifelse(is_vehicle, "0", as.character(layout$Conc))),
  HMSLid        = grid_of(fifelse(is_vehicle, "-", layout$HMSLid))
)

template_file <- file.path(prepared, "Template_20160421_308.xlsx")
writexl::write_xlsx(sheets, template_file, col_names = FALSE)

manifest <- data.table(
  Barcode       = plate_tab$Barcode,
  Template      = basename(template_file),
  clid          = "MCF10A",
  Duration      = NA_real_,
  plating_delay = plate_tab$plating_delay,
  T0date        = plate_tab$T0date
)
manifest_file <- file.path(prepared, "manifest_20160421.xlsx")
writexl::write_xlsx(manifest, manifest_file)

generate_datatable(manifest)


```

The `Duration` column is required by the manifest schema but stays empty here: for Incucyte
data the timepoints come from the `Elapsed` column of the results files, not from the manifest.

```{r layout_summary}
generate_datatable(
  layout[pert_type != "ctl_vehicle",
         .(n_wells = .N,
           n_conc = uniqueN(Conc),
           min_conc = min(Conc),
           max_conc = max(Conc)),
         by = .(DrugName, HMSLid)][order(DrugName)]
)


```

# Import

```{r load_data}
data_imported <- import_data(manifest_file,
                             template_file,
                             results_files,
                             instrument = "Incucyte")


```

```{r annotate}
drug_annotation_path <- file.path(wd, "data_annotation", "drug_annotation.csv")
drug_annotation <- if (file.exists(drug_annotation_path)) {
  fread(drug_annotation_path)
} else {
  get_drug_annotation_from_dt(data_imported)
}
data_imported <- annotate_dt_with_drug(data_imported, drug_annotation)
fwrite(drug_annotation, drug_annotation_path)
generate_datatable(drug_annotation)

cell_line_annotation_path <- file.path(wd, "data_annotation", "cell_line_annotation.csv")
cell_line_annotation <- if (file.exists(cell_line_annotation_path)) {
  fread(cell_line_annotation_path)
} else {
  get_cellline_annotation_from_dt(data_imported)
}
data_imported <- annotate_dt_with_cell_line(data_imported, cell_line_annotation)
fwrite(cell_line_annotation, cell_line_annotation_path)
generate_datatable(cell_line_annotation)

qs_save(data_imported, file.path(wd, "gDR_data", "gDR_input.qs2"))


```

MCF10A is not in the annotation catalogue shipped with gDR, so the cell line fields stay
`unknown`. That is cosmetic — nothing downstream in this example depends on them.

# What the import produced

```{r shape}
data.table(
  Metric = c("rows", "plates", "wells per plate", "timepoints", "drugs",
             "vehicle wells per plate", "elapsed range (h)"),
  Value = c(
    format(nrow(data_imported), big.mark = " "),
    uniqueN(data_imported$Barcode),
    uniqueN(data_imported[, paste0(WellRow, WellColumn)]),
    uniqueN(data_imported$Duration),
    uniqueN(data_imported[Gnumber != "vehicle"]$Gnumber),
    sum(layout$pert_type == "ctl_vehicle"),
    paste(range(data_imported$Duration), collapse = " - ")
  )
) |> generate_datatable()


```

```{r summary}
print(dfSummary(data_imported,
                varnumbers = FALSE,
                valid.col = FALSE,
                graph.magnif = 0.8,
                max.distinct.values = 50,
                max.string.width = 50,
                display.labels = FALSE),
      method = "render")


```

# Conclusion

The six plates are imported and annotated, and the result is saved to
`gDR_data/gDR_input.qs2`. Report 2 handles the timepoint grid — which needs attention before
anything is normalized — and runs the time-course processing.
